judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in "any other products and services offered by Angie's List at any time" after a specific enumeration, and contains a mechanical garble ("vouchers, ordeals" for "or deals"), leaving the reach of "Service" uncertain. Both features give a court something to construe about what the defined term covers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The statement that the Agreement may be modified "at our sole discretion" with notice sits alongside Section 19, which makes modifications effective immediately on posting, and alongside the incorporation of "linked" terms that Section 29's entire-agreement clause disclaims. That is a real, if modest, fit problem across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The affirmative statement that ratings are "based upon the actual first-hand experiences other users have had" is an operative-sounding description whose status (promise or mere description) and scope are readily contestable. The phrase "based upon" does not say ratings are exclusively or unmanipulatedly so derived.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This representation runs directly against Section 13 ("does not guarantee the accuracy, integrity, quality"; "passive conduit") and the Section 24 warranty disclaimer, so a court must reconcile a described service with global disclaimers of it. That is exactly the kind of whole-instrument tension a member suit would exploit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "In good standing" is undefined and "cone-year period" is a mechanical corruption of "one-year period," both bearing on when Redeemable Benefits vest. The unilateral "right to modify the Plans at any time and in its sole discretion" is also unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The promise that grandfathered subscriptions "will maintain the same services that are currently provided" is hard to square with the same paragraph's reservation of a right to modify Plans at will, and with Section 6's right to modify Membership Fees. That internal pull is genuine though not dramatic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation to provide "true, accurate, current and complete" registration information and keep it updated is a conventional, definite representation with no catch-all tail. Nothing here has a second reasonable reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with Section 16(F) and (T) on impersonation and false contact information; no other provision cuts against it. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single flat age requirement, "18 years of age or older," is as definite as drafting gets. No term requires construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16(A) warrants that the user is "above the age of eighteen (18)," which literally excludes exact eighteen-year-olds permitted here; the mismatch is trivial but real. Nothing else conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Void where prohibited" is a bare formula that identifies neither the prohibiting law nor the consequence of voidness, so its operation is genuinely indeterminate. It is short and vague in the way that invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits uneasily with the Section 30 choice of Indiana law "notwithstanding the choice of law provisions of the venue where any action is brought," but no direct contradiction emerges. Low-to-moderate relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple statement that a privacy policy exists at a stated URL; there is no operative promise to parse. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 29 declares this Agreement the entire agreement while the preamble and Section 16 rely on linked policies, but this clause itself only points to a document. Slight fit tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The all-caps sentence conditions renewal on cancellation, termination, or opting "OUT OF THE AUTOMATIC RENEWAL FEATURE AS PROVIDED BELOW," a cross-reference to a mechanism the document never supplies. That dangling reference is a mechanical/definitional defect bearing directly on renewal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reading it with the "Canceling Your Subscription" paragraph shows only cancellation, never an opt-out, so the promised opt-out cannot be located anywhere in the instrument. That is a concrete internal gap.
judgments.clause_name: 6. Service Fees and Billing Methods; Automatic Renewal

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The monthly renewal mechanics, timing ("on or about Your expiration date") and 180-day retry window are stated concretely; "standard renewal practices then in effect" is the only soft term. Overall definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 6's automatic-renewal announcement and the cancellation deadline; the 180-day retry does not contradict the cancellation paragraph. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Parallel to the monthly paragraph and equally concrete as to term, fee and retry period. No named ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The disclaimer of any pre-renewal notice sits against the Membership Renewals paragraph, which promises email notice before renewing a free-offer Additional List, but the two address different products. Minor tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "You formerly had to option to purchase access" is ungrammatical and its tense leaves unclear whether existing Additional List subscriptions still operate. The word "primary" is defined but its consequences are not stated here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6 still lists "Additional List Fees" as payable and the Membership Renewals paragraph still governs renewing an Additional List, which is awkward with a feature said to be only formerly available. That is a genuine reconciliation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Renewal "at the Membership Fee" is problematic where the member "received a free offer," because Membership Fee is defined as the amount actually charged excluding promotions. The clause also refers to cancelling access "in accordance with the provisions set forth below" without identifying them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the Section 6 definition of Membership Fee and against the Additional List paragraph's past tense, the renewal price for free-offer members is not determinable from the instrument. That is a specific incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The upgrade mechanics are internally confusing: it says you purchase "an additional annual subscription," then that "Your first subscription shall be upgraded," then that a "second subscription" begins later, and the heading itself is corrupted ("Down.rcLading"). The refund measure for downgrades ("the difference") is also unquantified as to proration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the once-annually Redeemable Benefit rule in Membership Benefits and with Section 18's pro rata refund on convenience termination without stating how the two subscriptions are treated. Moderate fit uncertainty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deadline (5:00 p.m. Eastern on the business day prior to the renewal payment date) and the three channels are specific and mechanical. Nothing invites construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the "CANCELLED" limb of Section 6's renewal sentence, though it does not supply the promised opt-out; the shortfall belongs to Section 6 rather than here. Largely consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence, that the magazine fee "is not deductible from Your Membership Fee," sits oddly with the preceding sentence that a portion of the Membership Fee is applied to the magazine, and "where applicable" is undefined. A reader could argue about refundability of the $6.50.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 offers the print magazine only "where available" in the member's market, which is not obviously the same as "where applicable" here, and Section 18's pro rata refund does not address the magazine portion. Mild relational uncertainty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The authorizations to revise expiration dates and to use a third-party card refresher are specific and consented to in plain terms. No named ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with the renewal paragraphs' reliance on "payment information on file" and with the Section 5 privacy policy reference. Consistent.
judgments.clause_name: 6. Authorization to Update Credit Card Account Information; Account Updater

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "You agree that You shall not bring any action against Angie's List relating in any way to the Incentives" is extremely broad and one-sided, and "otherwise incorrect, unfit, or unusable in any way" is a catch-all after specifics. A court could narrow either.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is of a piece with Sections 24 and 25's disclaimers and the Section 25 damages cap; no provision promises Incentives. Fits the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Members of Your household" is expressly defined as anyone currently sharing the registered address, which removes the obvious vagueness. Responsibility allocation is stated flatly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with Section 16(T)'s one-account rule and with Membership Benefits' "per household" limit on Redeemable Benefits. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition lists "access... visit or otherwise exploit for any commercial, educational, or any other non-personal purpose," a catch-all after specifics, and "visit" plus "access" appear to forbid the very conduct the sentence before licenses. That is both a general-vs-specific and an internal drafting tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16(Q) repeats the restriction but with a missing word, and Section 12's broad content license and Section 23's copyright claim overlap this grant; the boundary of permitted "personal purchase decisions" use is not settled anywhere. Moderate relational risk.
judgments.clause_name: 9. Limited License to Website and Magazine

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause depends on having "an active, qualifying Plan" without saying which Plans qualify, and one sentence breaks off mid-thought ("to discuss the issue with"). Both defects bear on entitlement to the CRP.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 lists CRP access only under the Premium Plan, so "qualifying Plan" must be read against that list, and the promise that a resolved review "will be removed" interacts with Section 12's irrevocable content license and Section 13's no-obligation-to-screen language. There is a specific cross-provision question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The licence grant is long but each verb and the scope (irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide) is spelled out; the only loose element is "all rights necessary to prohibit" third-party exploitation. Largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 16(R)'s duplicate grant and Section 23's ownership carve-out for user Content, which are consistent rather than conflicting; the CRP's removal of reviews is a minor counterpoint. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Passive conduit" and "interactive computer service provider" are legal characterisations the drafter asserts rather than facts, and the disclaimer of any guarantee of "accuracy, integrity, quality or appropriateness" is broad. A member could argue the characterisation cannot be self-conferred.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This directly opposes Section 1's statement that ratings are based on actual first-hand experiences, and Section 13 also reserves a right to review and delete Content, which sits awkwardly with passivity; Section 31's survival list omits Section 13. There is a real whole-instrument question.
judgments.clause_name: Section 13 — Publication and Distribution of Content

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The repeated parenthetical "which includes, but is not limited to, health care and wellness providers" is an open-ended gloss, but the disclaimer itself is comprehensive and clear in effect. Moderate-low textual risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Section 1's description of the vetting/ratings service and with Section 11's CRP assistance, which the CRP paragraph expressly says does not waive this section. The express non-waiver reduces, but does not remove, the tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Website Content" is defined as material contained on Angie's List's own Website, yet the section later says "If You post Website Content about services rendered to another individual," using the defined term for user postings. That definitional slippage changes what the representation covers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term collides with "Content" in Section 12 and "Copyright Materials" in Section 23, and the statement that posted health information "will not be protected by any federal or state laws" is qualified by "Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement" without identifying any such provision. Genuine cross-reference difficulty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (C) ends with "or racially, ethnically or otherwise objectionable" — a pure catch-all after a long list — (D) turns on the vague standard "thorough and thoughtful," and (Q) is missing a word ("purposes not related to... personal purchasing decisions, the express written consent"). Multiple named defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (A)'s "above the age of eighteen" does not match Section 3's "18 years of age or older," and (Q)/(P) overlap the Section 9 licence and Section 27's liquidated damages triggers. Moderate relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The consent to transfer information on a sale of assets is stated in ordinary terms, with "for any purpose allowed under this Agreement" tied to the document itself. Low textual risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Section 5 privacy policy for scope but does not contradict it or any other provision. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The initial term... will be defined in Your membership Plan" leaves the term to an extrinsic document, and "merely terminates Your account for its convenience" is an imprecise trigger for the pro rata refund. Moderate textual softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The refund obligation is hard to square with Section 20's blanket non-liability for discontinuing the Service and with Section 25's damages cap of one month's fees, which could be less than the pro rata refund owed. That is a specific cross-provision conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Modifications are "effective immediately upon being posted" while the next sentence promises "You will receive notice if modifications... are made," leaving unclear whether notice is a condition of effectiveness. That is an ambiguity about the modification mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same pairing appears in the preamble, and Section 6's right to modify fees mid-relationship depends on which reading prevails; the instrument never resolves the notice/effectiveness relationship. Moderate relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reservation to "limit access to, modify, change or discontinue the Service with or without notice" and to set unpublished "general practices, policies and limits" is broad and one-sidedly drafted, though its language is clear. The catch-all "including without limitation" list is illustrative only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A power to discontinue the Service with no liability is difficult to reconcile with Section 18's pro rata refund on termination and with the paid benefits promised in Section 1, since a member paying annually could lose everything without remedy. That is a real whole-instrument tension.
judgments.clause_name: 20. Modification, Limitation and Discontinuance of Service

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional disclaimer for internet-inherent delays; "inherent in the use of the Internet" is the only soft phrase. Low risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates part of Sections 24 and 25 without contradicting them. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section says the company will not "accept or consider" creative ideas yet provides that any such Submissions "will be the property of Angie's List," which is a tension within the clause itself. "Creative ideas, suggestions, or materials" is also an undefined boundary against welcomed "comments."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12 disclaims ownership of user-provided Content while this section claims outright ownership of Submissions, so the line between Content and Submissions matters and is not drawn. Moderate relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of "Copyright Materials" carves out user Content and lists categories with "including, but not limited to," a mild catch-all in an otherwise clear ownership statement. Low-to-moderate risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squares with Section 12's disclaimer of ownership of user Content and with Section 9's limited licence. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard "AS IS" language with an enumerated (A)-(E) list and a savings clause for jurisdictions barring implied-warranty disclaimers; the enumerated items are specific. Textually clear despite OCR noise ("THE SERVICE (S PROVIDED").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanket disclaimer must be read against Section 1's affirmative description of ratings drawn from actual first-hand experiences and against the paid-membership structure of Section 6, and Section 11 expressly preserves this section. That pairing is the natural battleground for a member claim.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion runs to "DIRECT" and "COMPENSATORY" damages and includes catch-alls "(F) ANY OTHER MATTER RELATING TO THE SERVICE" and "(G) ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT BY ANGIE'S LIST," so the list's specifics are swallowed by the general. A court would have to decide whether it leaves any remedy at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Excluding liability for the company's own breach conflicts with Section 18's promise of a pro rata refund and with Section 27(d)'s reservation of full remedies to Angie's List alone, leaving the bargain lopsided in a way that requires harmonisation. Specific conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap is arithmetically stated (one month, prorated) but is preceded by an asserted premise about "a substantial portion of the value You receive," and "liable for anything related to this Agreement" is very broad. The premise-plus-cap structure is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A one-month cap cannot comfortably coexist with Section 18's obligation to refund fees pro rata for the remainder of an annual term, nor with Section 27's $1,000-per-item liquidated damages running the other way. That asymmetry is a concrete whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(AS DEFINED HEREIN AND SUBJECT TO THE LIMITATIONS SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION SUFFERED BY YOU" is never closed, blurring which limitations attach to which damages. "Any other party involved in the credit card processing process" is also an open-ended class after specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is reinforced by Section 32's designation of the Released Parties as third-party beneficiaries and by the Section 25 cap it cross-references. Fits the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (c) covers "any intentional or willful violation of any rights of another or harm You may have caused to another," a very broad and undelimited trigger, and the indemnified group includes "users." Moderate textual breadth.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sole control of the defence sits alongside Sections 25 and 27 without contradiction, and the indemnity does not clash with any specific provision. Low relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The introductory recital that "damages are often difficult to calculate" is the stated justification for the stipulated sums, and it is triggered only "if it becomes necessary for Angie's List to pursue legal action," an imprecise condition. Both are contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (d) then provides for actual damages "to the extent such actual damages can be reasonably calculated," which undercuts the premise stated here; that is a direct internal tension. Specific conflict named.
judgments.clause_name: 27. Breach of Agreement and Liquidated Damages

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is any Content posted "in violation of this Agreement," which imports the whole vague conduct code of Section 16, and "We may (but shall not be required to) to issue You a warning" contains a duplicated word. Moderate risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section 16's standards (including "distasteful" and "thorough and thoughtful") to define the breach, and (d) refers to subsections "(a) through (c)" while these are lettered (A)-(C). Moderate relational untidiness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Exploit for any purpose" is a catch-all appended to a list of specific acts, and the sentence lacks its closing period; per-item quantification of "each item of Content" copied is also uncertain. Moderate risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps (A) where an offending post is also a reproduction, and both draw their content from Section 9 and Section 16(P)-(Q), one of which is grammatically incomplete. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Each review or record that is aggregated, disrupted, damaged or otherwise affected" ends in an unbounded catch-all that governs the multiplier for the $100 figure. That is a live measurement ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 16(G)-(I) closely enough, though "otherwise affected" is broader than the conduct those subsections describe. Modest relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference to "subsections (a) through (c)" does not match the lettering actually used, and "to the extent such actual damages can be reasonably calculated" is an open standard. The specific-performance sentence also opens with "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That "notwithstanding" override runs against Section 25's limitation of liability and against the liquidated-damages premise in the Section 27 preamble that damages are difficult to calculate. Identifiable internal friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice channels in each direction and a deemed-delivery rule (earlier of verification or two business days) are stated precisely. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The address here omits "Street" given in the cancellation paragraph but is otherwise the same, and cancellation is separately governed by its own channels. Essentially consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The procedure is a close paraphrase of §512(c)(3) but extends a copyright statute's notice regime to "trademark" claims, and asks for notices that include "substantially the following." Mild vagueness in "substantially" and in the statutory mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports Section 13's right to delete Content and Section 23's copyright claims without contradicting them. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Constitutes the entire agreement" is standard, but the same clause concedes that "[a]dditional terms and conditions may exist between You and third parties," and the user warrants those do not interfere — an unusual and hard-to-apply warranty. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble requires acceptance of terms "in, and linked to, this Membership Agreement" and contemplates separate terms for other Angie's List sites, so the integration statement and the incorporation-by-link are in tension. That is a specific conflict with the opening paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It grants "exclusive jurisdiction" in Marion County, Indiana and then permits Angie's List, at its sole discretion, to sue elsewhere — the word "exclusive" contradicts the exception in the same sentence. The one-year limitations bar is otherwise clear but "arising out or related to" is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The one-year bar interacts with Section 31's survival list and with Section 27's remedies, but nothing squarely contradicts it elsewhere. Low-to-moderate relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Including, but not limited to, Sections 12, 14, 15, 17 and 23 through 31" is exactly the general catch-all against enumerated specifics that leaves survival scope uncertain. A party could argue expressio unius as to omitted sections.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notably Section 13 (Publication and Distribution of Content) is omitted although Sections 14 and 15 both cross-refer to it, and Section 32's third-party beneficiary term also falls outside the list. That omission creates a concrete reconciliation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The severability limb is unusually phrased — a court "should incorporate a similar provision that would be considered valid" — which is an indefinite instruction rather than a standard blue-pencil rule. Otherwise the anti-assignment, non-waiver and no-agency terms are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The third-party beneficiary designation matches the Released Parties defined in Section 25, and the anti-assignment term matches Section 16(O). Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closing acknowledgment of assent in unambiguous terms; nothing operative to construe beyond consent by use. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the preamble's acceptance language and does not conflict with Section 19's continued-use-as-acceptance rule. Consistent.
